source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 22:43 combines complete Hebrew 22:43–44. Public 22:44–53 bind Hebrew 22:45–54. Public 22:1–42 retain matching original records, including 22:21 and its question; its KJV annotation concerns a clause, not a whole-record renumbering.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the interval of peace.
verses.before: For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.
verses.after: For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.

verses.rationale: Identifies both kingdoms without inserting a motive.
verses.before: In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.
verses.after: In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Makes the reproach audible within the royal claim.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to his servants, “Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us? Yet we are keeping silent instead of taking it from the hand of the king of Aram.”
verses.after: Israel’s king said to his servants, “You know Ramoth-gilead belongs to us. Why are we doing nothing to take it back from the king of Aram?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to his servants, “Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us? Yet we are keeping silent instead of taking it from the hand of the king of Aram.”

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold pledge of solidarity.
verses.before: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”
verses.after: He asked Jehoshaphat, “Will you join me in battle at Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat answered Israel’s king, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the requested order of action.
verses.before: Yet Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire today for the word of the LORD.”
verses.after: But Jehoshaphat said to Israel’s king, “First, please seek the LORD’s word.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire today for the word of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps approximate count and Adonai designation.
verses.before: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, “Should I go against Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should I refrain?” They said, “Go up, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.”
verses.after: Israel’s king gathered about four hundred prophets and asked, “Should I go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or hold back?” “Go,” they said. “The Lord will give it into the king’s hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, “Should I go against Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should I refrain?” They said, “Go up, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.rationale: Preserves another prophet rather than denying all prophetic status.
verses.before: Yet Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?”
verses.after: Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no other prophet of the LORD here whom we can consult?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Ahab’s complaint from the narrator’s judgment.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say such a thing.”
verses.after: Israel’s king answered, “There is one more man through whom we can consult the LORD, Micaiah son of Imlah. But I hate him. He never prophesies good for me, only disaster.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not speak that way.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say such a thing.”

verses.rationale: Court role translated without settling bodily status.
verses.before: Then the king of Israel summoned one official and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”
verses.after: Then Israel’s king called a court official. “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Israel summoned one official and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”

verses.rationale: Makes the public setting clear.
verses.before: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, clothed in robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.after: Israel’s king and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by Samaria’s gate. All the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, clothed in robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

verses.rationale: Preserves enacted animal imagery and destruction.
verses.before: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made for himself horns of iron, and he said, “Thus says the LORD: With these you will gore Aram until you have destroyed them.”
verses.after: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself iron horns. He declared, “This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore Aram until you finish them off.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made for himself horns of iron, and he said, “Thus says the LORD: With these you will gore Aram until you have destroyed them.”

verses.rationale: Retains their united prediction and divine name.
verses.before: All the prophets prophesied so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”
verses.after: All the prophets said the same: “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed! The LORD will give it into the king’s hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the prophets prophesied so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.rationale: Exposes pressure to conform without adding motive.
verses.before: The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth favorable to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably.”
verses.after: The messenger who went to summon Micaiah told him, “The prophets are speaking with one voice in the king’s favor. Please let your word agree with theirs. Speak favorably.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth favorable to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably.”

verses.rationale: Keeps oath and stated prophetic obligation.
verses.before: Yet Micaiah said, “As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, that I will speak.”
verses.after: Micaiah answered, “As the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Micaiah said, “As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, that I will speak.”

verses.rationale: Leaves apparent irony to the following exchange.
verses.before: When he came to the king, the king said to him, “Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should we refrain?” He said to him, “Go up and prosper, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”
verses.after: When he reached the king, the king asked, “Micaiah, should we go to war at Ramoth-gilead, or hold back?” He answered, “Go and succeed! The LORD will give it into the king’s hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When he came to the king, the king said to him, “Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should we refrain?” He said to him, “Go up and prosper, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the king’s challenge and oath language.
verses.before: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear that you will tell me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?”
verses.after: The king replied, “How many times must I put you under oath to tell me only the truth in the LORD’s name?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear that you will tell me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the shepherd image and peace announcement.
verses.before: Then he said, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd.” And the LORD said, “These have no master. Let each return to their house in peace.”
verses.after: Then Micaiah said, “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, ‘These have no master. Let each return home in peace.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd.” And the LORD said, “These have no master. Let each return to their house in peace.”

verses.rationale: Repeats Ahab’s accusation as his interpretation.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”
verses.after: Israel’s king said to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you? He prophesies nothing good for me, only disaster.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the heavenly council distinct from earthly thrones.
verses.before: Micaiah said, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing beside him, on his right and on his left.
verses.after: Micaiah continued, “Then hear the LORD’s word. I saw the LORD seated on his throne, with all heaven’s army standing beside him, to his right and left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Micaiah said, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing beside him, on his right and on his left.

verses.rationale: Retains divine initiative in the disturbing vision.
verses.before: The LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One said one thing, and another said another.
verses.after: The LORD asked, ‘Who will entice Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One proposed this, another that.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One said one thing, and another said another.

verses.rationale: Uses the full original Hebrew record, including the question.
verses.before: Then the spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The LORD said to him, ‘How?’
verses.after: Then the spirit came forward and stood before the LORD. ‘I will entice him,’ it said. ‘How?’ the LORD asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The LORD said to him, ‘How?’

verses.rationale: Preserves authorization of deception without theological repair.
verses.before: He said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And he said, ‘You will entice him, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.’
verses.after: It answered, ‘I will go and become a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ The LORD said, ‘You will entice him and succeed. Go and do it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And he said, ‘You will entice him, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the vision’s application attributed to Micaiah.
verses.before: Now look: the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours; and the LORD has spoken evil concerning you.”
verses.after: So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now look: the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours; and the LORD has spoken evil concerning you.”

verses.rationale: Retains the blow and derisive question.
verses.before: Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek. He said, “Which way did the spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?”
verses.after: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek. “Which way did the LORD’s spirit pass from me to speak to you?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek. He said, “Which way did the spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?”

verses.rationale: Keeps future answer without adding its occasion.
verses.before: Micaiah said, “Look, you will see on that day when you go from room to room to hide yourself.”
verses.after: Micaiah answered, “You will see on the day you go into an inner room to hide.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Micaiah said, “Look, you will see on that day when you go from room to room to hide yourself.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both custodians and Joash’s title.
verses.before: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon, governor of the city, and to Joash, the king’s son.
verses.after: Israel’s king said, “Take Micaiah back to Amon the city governor and Joash the king’s son.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon, governor of the city, and to Joash, the king’s son.

verses.rationale: Makes the deprivation concrete and repeats peace.
verses.before: Say, ‘Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction until I come in peace.’”
verses.after: Tell them, ‘The king says: Put this man in prison. Give him meager bread and water until I return in peace.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Say, ‘Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction until I come in peace.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the public challenge and broad final address.
verses.before: Micaiah said, “If you indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken through me.” And he said, “Hear, all you peoples!”
verses.after: Micaiah said, “If you really return in peace, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Listen, all you peoples!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Micaiah said, “If you indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken through me.” And he said, “Hear, all you peoples!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrative resumption spare.
verses.before: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.after: Israel’s king and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.rationale: Clarifies who disguises himself without supplying a scheme.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and enter the battle, but you wear your robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.
verses.after: Israel’s king told Jehoshaphat, “I will enter the battle in disguise, but you wear your robes.” So Israel’s king disguised himself and went into battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and enter the battle, but you wear your robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.

verses.rationale: Retains exact command and number.
verses.before: Now the king of Aram had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, “Do not fight with small or great, but only with the king of Israel.”
verses.after: The king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, “Fight no one, small or great, except the king of Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king of Aram had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, “Do not fight with small or great, but only with the king of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Does not invent the words of his cry.
verses.before: When the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “Surely this is the king of Israel.” So they turned aside to fight against him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.after: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “That must be Israel’s king!” They turned to attack him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “Surely this is the king of Israel.” So they turned aside to fight against him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition as the stated reason.
verses.before: When the commanders of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.
verses.after: When they saw he was not Israel’s king, they stopped pursuing him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the commanders of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

verses.rationale: Preserves untargeted shot and uncertain armor detail.
verses.before: But a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the scale armor and the breastplate. He said to his charioteer, “Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded.”
verses.after: But a man drew his bow without a particular target and struck Israel’s king between the armor’s fittings and breastplate. The king told his chariot driver, “Turn around and take me out of the fighting. I am wounded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the scale armor and the breastplate. He said to his charioteer, “Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded.”

verses.rationale: Retains bodily injury and continued exposure.
verses.before: The battle grew fierce that day, and the king was held upright in his chariot facing Aram. He died in the evening, and the blood from the wound flowed into the hollow of the chariot.
verses.after: The battle grew fierce that day. The king was held upright in his chariot facing Aram. He died that evening, and blood from his wound ran into the chariot’s floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The battle grew fierce that day, and the king was held upright in his chariot facing Aram. He died in the evening, and the blood from the wound flowed into the hollow of the chariot.

verses.rationale: Keeps the twofold dismissal.
verses.before: At the setting of the sun, a cry passed through the camp: “Each to their city, and each to their land!”
verses.after: At sunset a shout went through the camp: “Everyone to his town! Everyone to his own land!”
verses.tsw_comparator: At the setting of the sun, a cry passed through the camp: “Each to their city, and each to their land!”

verses.rationale: Clarifies transport of the dead king.
verses.before: So the king died and was brought to Samaria. They buried the king in Samaria.
verses.after: The king was dead. They brought him to Samaria and buried him there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king died and was brought to Samaria. They buried the king in Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains prostitutes and location without harmonizing Naboth’s oracle.
verses.before: They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, while the prostitutes washed themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken.
verses.after: They washed the chariot at Samaria’s pool, where prostitutes bathed, and dogs licked his blood, just as the LORD had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, while the prostitutes washed themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source notice and ivory house.
verses.before: Now the rest of the deeds of Ahab, all that he did, the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Ahab’s deeds, everything he did, the ivory house he built, and all the towns he built—are they not written in the annals of the kings of Israel?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the deeds of Ahab, all that he did, the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keeps the ancestral death formula.
verses.before: Ahab lay down with his ancestors, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.after: Ahab lay down with his ancestors, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab lay down with his ancestors, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

verses.rationale: Retains the regnal synchronism.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves age, reign, and maternal lineage.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

verses.rationale: Binds both Hebrew records 43–44 to the inherited public label.
verses.before: He walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD. Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
verses.after: He followed the whole course of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the LORD’s eyes. Yet the high places remained; the people still sacrificed and burned offerings there.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD. Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

verses.rationale: Retains peace between the kingdoms.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source referral and military record.
verses.before: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoshaphat, his might that he showed, and how he fought—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
verses.after: The rest of Jehoshaphat’s deeds, his achievements, and the wars he fought—are they not written in the annals of the kings of Judah?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoshaphat, his might that he showed, and how he fought—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

verses.rationale: Matches the qualified cult-term choice in earlier chapters.
verses.before: He removed from the land the rest of the male cult prostitutes who remained in the days of Asa his father.
verses.after: He removed from the land the remaining male shrine attendants who had survived from his father Asa’s days.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removed from the land the rest of the male cult prostitutes who remained in the days of Asa his father.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinction without identifying an overlord.
verses.before: There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.
verses.after: There was no king in Edom; a deputy ruled as king.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.

verses.rationale: Follows the read forms and keeps the failed voyage.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, for the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat built Tarshish ships to sail to Ophir for gold. But they never sailed, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, for the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.

verses.rationale: Does not import a different sequence from Chronicles.
verses.before: Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.” But Jehoshaphat was unwilling.
verses.after: Then Ahaziah son of Ahab told Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants sail with yours.” But Jehoshaphat refused.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.” But Jehoshaphat was unwilling.

verses.rationale: Clarifies ancestral David rather than immediate father.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his father. Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David his ancestor. His son Jehoram became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his father. Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserves both chronological statements.
verses.before: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
verses.after: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

verses.rationale: Retains the three influences and corporate consequence.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father, in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: He did evil in the LORD’s eyes, following his father, his mother, and Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father, in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Closes with worship, anger, and continuity.
verses.before: He served Baal and bowed down to him, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, just as his father had done.
verses.after: He served Baal and bowed down to him, provoking the LORD, Israel’s God, just as his father had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He served Baal and bowed down to him, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, just as his father had done.

comparative_references.scope: All 53 TSW verses read after drafting independently from every pinned Hebrew verse and its source notes.
